title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-08-06 comparing programmatic tool calling to JSON tool calling across 14 models on BFCL v4
problem: Tool-calling agents emit structured JSON objects for each function call, requiring precise argument serialization, multi-step chaining, and fan-out across heterogeneous APIs. For code-capable models, JSON format is a design choice not a necessity. Whether programmatic tool calling matches JSON tool calling across model families and adversarial context loads remained untested.
mechanism: Programmatic tool calling (PTC) exposes tools as typed Python stubs that the model invokes through code, with execution and results handled in a single agent turn via shell subprocess. The agent loop executes the script without additional inference turns. JSON tool calling requires separate inference turns per function call.

evidence.claim: GPT-5.6 family achieves 10.6% improvement over JSON tool calling baseline on BFCL v4
evidence.condition: BFCL v4 subset (309 entries, eight categories)

evidence.claim: Programmatic tool calling matches or exceeds baseline in 13 of 14 models under parallel fan-out
evidence.condition: Parallel fan-out testing, Claude Sonnet 5 N=100 maintains 100% enumeration accuracy vs. 0% for JSON

evidence.claim: JSON tool calling drops tool calls entirely at N=70-72 (Claude Sonnet 5)
Programmatic tool calling holds stable under context rot while JSON tool calling degrades 2.3% on average
evidence.condition: Context flood (128 schemas) vs filtered (relevant only), n=31 per condition

evidence.claim: Chaining entries complete in 0.32-0.96 of baseline latency for 13 of 14 models
evidence.condition: Sequential chaining tasks, single inference turn vs. two turns for JSON

evaluation_context: Evaluated on BFCL v4 subset (309 entries, eight categories: simple_python, multiple, parallel, parallel multiple, live_simple, live_multiple, live_parallel, live parallel multiple). 14 models tested (5 Anthropic: Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, 4.6, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5; 9 OpenAI: GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5-nano, GPT-5, GPT-5.4-mini, 5.4, 5.6-Luna/ Sol/Terra). Ab studies: fan-out enumeration, chaining, context rot (filtered vs. 128-schema flood).
limitations: BFCL v4 uses echo-return stubs (returns arguments verbatim, not real API calls) - measures argument serialization accuracy, not end-to-end tool-use correctness. Ablation entry counts small (n=31-52 per condition) with wide confidence intervals. 20% evaluator-human misalignment found in BFCL v4's LLM-judge mode (deterministic scorer avoids this). Programmatic tool calling has 1.5x input token overhead vs JSON on chaining. Results may not transfer to settings where return values affect downstream calls.
project_relevance: Programmatic tool calling reduces agent tool execution latency by eliminating per-call inference turns (0.32-0.96x chaining latency). Maintains 100% accuracy under high fan-out (N=100) where JSON tool calling fails entirely. Robust under context flooding (+5.5% vs. -2.3% degradation). For Agent semantic acceleration, this addresses tool call overhead specifically but does not directly reduce Read/Grep/repository search operations. The method is relevant for optimizing tool execution chains in agents, particularly for parallel operations and chaining scenarios. However, the paper does not report Read次数, Grep次数, token consumption beyond input overhead, or task success rates beyond BFCL accuracy.
